title: 'FIRE' Movement Helps People Retire Early
paragraphs: Most people expect to work until they are around 65 years old. But followers of the "FIRE" movement hope to stop working much earlier, sometimes even in their 30s or 40s.
FIRE stands for "Financial Independence, Retire Early." The basic idea is to save and invest enough money so that working becomes a choice rather than a necessity.

To reach this goal, people following the FIRE movement often save a very large part of their income. While people saving for a traditional retirement might save 10% to 15% of their income, FIRE followers often save 50% to 70%, or even more. They usually cut their spending, live simply, and invest their savings, often in low-cost index funds.

FIRE followers often use two simple rules. The first is the "25x rule," which says that you need to save about 25 times the amount you spend each year. The second is the "4% rule," which suggests that if you take out no more than 4% of your savings each year, your money should last for a very long time.

Some people choose a more flexible version. For example, with "Coast FIRE," people save enough early in life that their investments can grow on their own, so they can later work less. Others continue to do part-time or flexible work after reaching financial independence.

However, FIRE is not easy for most people. Saving half of your income usually requires a high salary. Early retirees also need to pay for their own health insurance and plan carefully, because their money may need to last 40 or 50 years. Some people who retire early also say they feel bored or lose their sense of purpose, and some return to work.
Rising prices are also making FIRE harder. In a survey of 1,000 American workers by MyPerfectResume in May 2026, 71% said that FIRE is now unrealistic for most people.
